If this means John Austin, the legal positivist, the label fits because he treated law as observable facts: commands from a determinate sovereign backed by sanctions, habitually obeyed. He modelled that on a simple, sovereign-centred legal system that has since become obsolete, so the theory doesn't fit modern systems with constitutional limits, power-conferring rules and no single sovereign. I'm inferring the reasoning from your team note rather than from a source that uses the exact phrase "naive empiricist."
